selected_evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs
selected_evidence.summary: Shows the exact two-entry allow-list, secure metadata, active crond service, successful authorization for root and opsadmin, and explicit denial for an unlisted user.

selected_evidence.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel
selected_evidence.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 are identical before and after the change and reboot.

Captures the healthy baseline, acknowledged native reboot, changed boot ID from e9250ad1-c4f0-4bec-b58e-4e30255a8dcf to 67963bd1-f094-4a1c-ac9e-0d5384fdefbf, and recovered crond service, accounts, access-control file, and authorization behavior.

commands.command:
set -eu
printf '%s\n' '--- OS ---'
cat /etc/redhat-release
uname -r
printf '%s\n' '--- boot ---'
cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
printf '%s\n' '--- cron access files ---'
for f in /etc/cron.allow /etc/cron.deny; do
  if [ -e "$f" ]; then ls -l "$f"; sed -n '1,80p' "$f"; else printf '%s missing\n' "$f"; fi
done
printf '%s\n' '--- users ---'
getent passwd root opsadmin || true
printf '%s\n' '--- crond health ---'
systemctl is-enabled crond
systemctl is-active crond
systemctl --no-pager --full status crond | sed -n '1,12p'
printf '%s\n' '--- root crontab ---'
crontab -u root -l 2>&1 || true
printf '%s\n' '--- opsadmin crontab ---'
crontab -u opsadmin -l 2>&1 || true

commands.command:
set -eu
if ! getent passwd opsadmin >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo -n useradd -m -s /bin/bash opsadmin; fi
printf 'root\nopsadmin\n' > /tmp/cron.allow.antrieb
sudo -n install -o root -g root -m 0600 /tmp/cron.allow.antrieb /etc/cron.allow
sudo -n restorecon /etc/cron.allow 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f /tmp/cron.allow.antrieb
printf '%s\n' 'cron access configuration applied'
getent passwd opsadmin
sudo -n ls -lZ /etc/cron.allow
sudo -n sed -n '1,20p' /etc/cron.allow
